title: Six figures from OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber post
intro: Move across six lines from OpenAI’s 5 November 2026 post. Each stop is one evaluation or one count the post prints. The page does not turn a percent into a ranking, and it does not put the model in ChatGPT.
note: Every figure on the control is from OpenAI’s post "GPT-6 Cyber," dated 5 November 2026. ExploitGym is the post’s test of whether a model can exploit a specified vulnerability: 48.5 percent, up from 32.1 percent for GPT-5.6 Cyber. The post calls that a 51 percent relative improvement and about 16 percentage points. This control does not subtract the two scores itself. The scope line is ExploitGym Honeypot. 99.93 percent is without deployment safety prompts. 100 percent is with those prompts. 94.49 percent is GPT-5.6 Cyber without those prompts. The web line is a new evaluation in the same post. 40.3 percent recall, against 32.0 percent for GPT-6 Astra. The post says the models did not have source code. RemoteExploitBench, as the post describes it, uses known vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. 95 percent is how many tasks GPT-6 Cyber completed. 100 percent is how many GPT-6 Astra, running with Daybreak Blue, refused. The Linux counts are 948 exploits, 166 for GPT-5.6 Sol on the same research harness, 1,724 vulnerabilities reproduced, and 304 critical findings disclosed with candidate patches. The Firefox counts are 81 novel vulnerabilities the post says Mozilla classified as high severity, and 30 known issues the post says were more severe than previously reported. None of these figures is an outside lab’s rerun. The system card is not on this control. The post does not say GPT-6 Cyber is in ChatGPT.
